title: The Singer and the Druggist

full_text:
In Cairo lived an impoverished young lutenist named Salim and an elderly apothecary named Master Yusuf. For five years, when Salim had neither pupils nor concerts, Yusuf shared his daily bread, gave him herbal tonics when he was feverish, and encouraged him to practice his scales in the back of the shop.

When Salim’s genius was finally recognized by the Governor of Alexandria, he became the most celebrated musician in Egypt, receiving rich rewards of gold and estates.

Salim immediately returned to Cairo, bought the building where the apothecary’s shop stood, and presented the deed to Master Yusuf, along with a thousand gold dinars:

'Master, you sustained my breath when the world had no ear for my song; half of everything I create belongs to your generous heart.'

The two friends remained inseparable, proving that gratitude is the sweetest harmony of life.
moral: True friendship supports artistic dreams during the winter of obscurity.
